persona: Simulated instrumentalist new to DAWs, seeking a short melodic instrumental

outcome.status: Project saved and WAV/MIDI exports visibly confirmed; audio quality not auditioned
outcome.composition: Four-bar C minor quarter-note melody drawn with the mouse, repeated over Circuit rhythm stock audio; final clips trimmed to fourteen bars at 112 BPM.
outcome.audio_used: Circuit rhythm stock audio on Circuit drums track
outcome.midi_instrument: Rill Lab Sine, native VST3 instrument
outcome.name_entered_with: Built-in on-screen keyboard operated by mouse
outcome.export_settings_visible: Arrangement 0:30.000; 48 kHz; stereo; 32-bit float; effect tails unchecked
outcome.playback_caveat: First playback advanced and showed track meters but reported Plug-in/render error, 89 failures. Followed the visible stop-and-restart instruction. No sound-quality claim.
outcome.final_playback_observation: Final playback reached the end and stopped with no new visible render-error banner. Earlier error remains unexplained; no audio audition.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Blank-lane MIDI hint, instrument assignment, note lengths, and clip duplication made the core task manageable. Discovering note editing and correcting trim endpoints took extra attempts.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Consistent dark interface, teal waveforms, readable transport, and miniature melody previews looked polished. The piano keys and background grid could offer clearer musical guidance.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most mouse actions responded promptly; reached a complete saved/exported arrangement in roughly six minutes of app interaction. Playback preparation and native dialogs introduced brief waits. This is perceived workflow speed, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Moderate confusion: double-clicking the MIDI clip had no visible effect, sharps were used in a minor-key grid, and a render-error message did not explain the failed component or whether the export was affected.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The tested scope included real VST assignment, piano roll, audio/MIDI arrangement, trimming, mouse naming, project save, and both exports. Playback error limits confidence in the whole audio workflow; other instruments and advanced features were not evaluated.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the new MIDI pattern did not visibly open the note editor. Right-click exposed Edit notes and worked.
findings.recommendation: Make the primary note-edit action visible on a selected MIDI clip or explain the supported gesture. Verify double-click behavior in the actual app.

findings.observation: The piano roll names notes after entry, but most piano-key rows are unlabeled. C Natural minor was the grid scale, yet Eb and Bb appeared as D# and A#.
findings.recommendation: Offer clearer key labels and scale-aware note spelling for musicians learning the grid.

findings.observation: Trimming against the seconds ruler first produced 30.268 seconds, then 29.732, before a small correction reached 30.000. The displayed duration made correction possible.
findings.recommendation: Show the exact proposed clip end time during edge dragging and provide an accessible numeric endpoint control.

findings.observation: Playback advanced and meters were active, but a bottom banner reported Plug-in/render error, 89 failures. Details repeated the instruction to stop and restart and listed 48 kHz/1024 frames. A final playback pass reached the end and stopped without a new visible error banner.
findings.recommendation: Identify the failed plug-in or render stage, explain whether playback is partial, and distinguish recovered playback from a still-active error. Evaluate the underlying cause separately from this lab observation.

findings.observation: Rename project offered a clickable keyboard, allowing a chosen title without hardware keyboard input. Save and exports reused the title automatically.
findings.recommendation: Retain this mouse-complete naming flow and make it available consistently wherever text entry is needed.

findings.observation: WAV export summarized duration and format, provided a tails checkbox, then showed an Exported confirmation. MIDI export likewise confirmed success.
findings.recommendation: Keep the clear export summary and completion feedback; consider showing the saved destination directly alongside Copy path.

positives: Double-click for MIDI hint led directly to the installed instrument library.
Assign instrument created both a track and an editable pattern with a visible VST label.
Quarter-note length selection and automatic clip growth made a melody quick to draw.
Clip Duplicate placed repetitions sequentially without manual positioning.
Bars and seconds were shown together; total project duration was always visible.
Mouse keyboard allowed a chosen project name.
Save and both export operations could be completed entirely with the mouse.
limitations: This is an independent simulated beginner session, not human-subject research.
Only visible UI and mouse input were used; no source, project data, prior reports, or peer sessions were inspected.
Audio was not auditioned. Active meters and successful export banners do not prove audible quality or complete VST rendering.
The coordinator must independently verify saved project structure, WAV duration/PCM, and MIDI content.
Only supplied stock audio and the actual native laboratory Rill Lab Sine VST were exercised; no conclusions about other plug-ins.
Software graphics, timer-paced virtual audio with 60 ms buffering, 1024-frame requests at 48 kHz, and absent window manager limit hardware and dialog-positioning conclusions.
The musical arrangement is a simple repeated melody, not a developed production or mix.
